subject: botany_2
question_text: For which variety of Indian rice has a patent been filed by a USA company?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.46, printed question 122. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: One word answers the question. The second mark comes from saying what a biopiracy case is.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The variety
steps.margin_note: Name the variety and say what it is. Four lines.
lines: A patent was filed by an American company on
Basmati is a long grained, aromatic rice grown
for centuries in the Indian subcontinent.
steps.why: Basmati was already a traditional crop, so a patent on it claimed ownership of something that had been developed communally over centuries.
common_mistakes: Naming Jaya or Ratna. Those are semi-dwarf HIGH YIELDING varieties, not the patent case.
Giving the name with no context. One line on what basmati is helps.
steps.memory_tip: Basmati: the aromatic one, and the patented one.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.margin_note: Name biopiracy and define it. Six lines.

lines.text: Patenting a traditional variety is BIOPIRACY

lines: Patenting a variety that a country has developed
and used for centuries is called BIOPIRACY.
It is the use of bio-resources or traditional
steps.why: A patent gives exclusive rights, so patenting a traditional variety would let one company charge for something a whole region already owned.
common_mistakes: Not naming biopiracy. It is the term the case is famous for.
Saying a patent was granted permanently. The case was contested.
steps.memory_tip: Taking what was already communally owned.
